core_classification.analysis: Lucien explicitly presents his former love for Louise as a past emotional state: “comme je t’aimais” (“how I loved you”). The utterance makes no relational commitment or undertaking. Although emphatic and accompanied by tears, it is deliberately staged rather than depicted as an affect-driven verbal discharge, so it does not independently support E.
core_classification.ambiguity: The sincerity and present emotional basis of the avowal are doubtful, but this does not alter its strong truth-conditional mode.

utterance_status.description: Lucien directly whispers the past-tense love avowal to Louise within narrated dialogue.

contextual_interpretation: The avowal forms part of a calculated theatrical performance. Lucien adopts an operatic pose, deliberately produces tears, and speaks precisely when he sees that Louise has noticed them. This strongly suggests strategic seduction or manipulation, though the words still present former love as true. His subsequent invocation of recovered memories and youthful illusions leaves some possibility that real feeling accompanies the performance.

evidence.supports: The explicit past-tense avowal strongly supports T: Lucien presents former love for Louise as an emotional fact.

evidence.quotation_or_description: Lucien assumes operatic attitudes and gestures and “trouva moyen de se faire venir un peu de larmes dans les yeux.”
evidence.supports: The tears and emotional presentation are deliberately manufactured, weighing against interpreting the words as a reflex-like expressive discharge.

evidence.quotation_or_description: He speaks “au moment où il vit que ses larmes avaient été vues par la comtesse.”
evidence.supports: The timing is calculated for effect on Louise, reinforcing strategic avowal rather than E and supplying no relational undertaking for P.

evidence.quotation_or_description: “j’ai retrouvé pour un moment mes souvenirs, mes illusions, mes vingt ans”
evidence.supports: His follow-up frames the avowal as recollection of a former emotional life, while leaving uncertain whether genuine feeling coexists with the performance.

ontology_assessment.diagnosis: T naturally captures the avowal of a past loving state. Its theatricality, possible insincerity, and manipulative purpose are contextual features rather than missing dimensions of core force; neither P, E, nor O is needed.

notes: The exclamation, whispering, tears, and emotional imagery do not independently establish E, especially because the passage explicitly depicts their calculated production.
